title: NASA's higher-resolution Mars images released to calm the controversy
summary: Tim Alberino tells of NASA's higher-resolution Mars images released to calm the controversy, about 1990s–2000s at Cydonia, Mars / NASA, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: that NASA um released those second higher resolution images to sort of quell the the firestorm that had erupted.

plain: Tim Alberino, a researcher and filmmaker, talks about Cydonia, a region of Mars where some see a "face" and other shapes that look built. He says that in the 1990s and 2000s NASA, the US space agency, released a second set of sharper images of the area to calm the uproar that had broken out over those shapes. In his telling, the new pictures were meant to settle the argument over whether anything artificial is on Mars.
